_meta.indication: Zydelig is indicated, in combination with rituximab, for the treatment of patients with relapsed chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) for whom rituximab alone would be considered appropriate therapy due to other co-morbidities; and for relapsed follicular B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (FL) and relapsed small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) in patients who have received at least two prior systemic therapies.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of idelalisib plus rituximab versus placebo plus rituximab
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with relapsed CLL who required treatment and were unable to tolerate standard chemotherapy due to coexisting medical conditions, reduced renal function (creatinine clearance <60 mL/min), or Grade ≥3 neutropenia or thrombocytopenia from prior myelotoxic therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival (PFS) as assessed by the Independent Review Committee (IRC)
pivotal_trials.n: 220 subjects randomized (110 idelalisib + rituximab; 110 placebo + rituximab)
pivotal_trials.result: Median PFS not reached (idelalisib + rituximab) vs 5.5 months (placebo + rituximab); HR 0.18 (95% CI 0.10, 0.32); p < 0.0001. Overall response rate 74.5% vs 14.5%.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%): diarrhea, pyrexia, fatigue, nausea, cough, pneumonia, abdominal pain, chills, and rash. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 49% of Zydelig + rituximab subjects, most frequently pneumonia (17%), pyrexia (9%), sepsis (8%), febrile neutropenia (5%) and diarrhea (5%). Grade 3/4 neutropenia occurred in 31% of patients.
target_moa: Idelalisib is an inhibitor of PI3Kδ (phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase delta), which is expressed in normal and malignant B-cells; it induces apoptosis and inhibits proliferation and B-cell receptor signaling.

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for fatal and serious toxicities: hepatic, severe diarrhea, colitis, pneumonitis, and intestinal perforation. Fatal and/or serious hepatotoxicity occurred in 14% and fatal and/or serious severe diarrhea or colitis occurred in 14% of Zydelig-treated patients.

rems.type: A REMS consisting of a communication plan and a timetable for submission of assessments is required to ensure the benefits outweigh the risks of fatal and serious events including hepatotoxicity, severe diarrhea or colitis, pneumonitis, and intestinal perforation.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the drug.

summary.text: Idelalisib (Zydelig) for relapsed CLL received a regular (not accelerated) approval under a priority review of NDA 206545, supported by Fast Track and Orphan Drug designations. Regular approval was based on the single randomized, placebo-controlled trial Study 312-0116 demonstrating a significant improvement in progression-free survival for idelalisib plus rituximab versus rituximab alone.
